explanation: Read PolicyProcessing.vb 383-398 (supEntryMet). Two claims fall short. (1) Only an entry marked as a version range reaches the child-product branch: a plain entry (IsRange False, no min/max, AdmxFile.vb:57) naming a parent product that is not itself ticked is also met when any ticked child or grandchild exists, because line 387-388 default the range to 0..highest child version. State both: a plain entry is met by its own product ticked, or, for a parent product, by any ticked child or grandchild; a range entry is never met by its own product being ticked, only by a ticked child or grandchild within min..max (open ends default to 0 and the highest child version), and nothing deeper than grandchildren counts; a range entry on a product with no children is never met. (2) 'With no product ticked, no entry is met' is false for an entry that names no product: line 383 returns the blank-support option's value for it, so with nothing ticked and that option ticked such an entry is met. Reword to 'no entry naming a product is met'.

The first two cases (no support definition, blank definition) decide the whole policy at line 381, so 'pass / refused' is exact for them. An entry naming no product is different: line 383 only makes that one entry met or unmet, and the policy outcome still comes from the combination of its entries (lines 393-415). Ticked, such an entry counts as met, so the policy passes if any entry is met, or, where the 'at least one selected product' option makes an all-of definition need every entry, only if all are. Unticked, the entry counts as unmet and the policy is refused only when no other entry is met (or, for an all-of definition under the other option, because this one fails). Rewrite the third case as an entry-level effect, not a policy pass/refusal.

'Every quoted phrase appears as consecutive whole words' and 'words are split on spaces, carriage returns and line feeds' hold only for plain and wildcard words. Phrases are tested on the cleaned text with spaces as the only boundary (lines 56-57: contains ' phrase ', starts with 'phrase ', ends with ' phrase', or equals it), and the text is trimmed of spaces only. So a phrase next to or across a line break is not found (a phrase whose last word is followed by a line break, or whose first word follows one, does not match unless a space also sits there). Say so, so a tester can try a phrase against multi-line description text.
